issues.description: Element: SealSaloon.stock (field). Problem statement is contradictory about whether stock is an instance field initialized in the no-argument constructor vs a class-level shared field: the task text (instructions about initializing attributes in the constructor) implies stock should be initialized in the instance constructor, while a separate note explicitly states "stock attribute: This is shared across all instances" and lists stock as required to be static. The reference solution declares stock as a static field (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()). This conflict (instance-initialized vs static/shared) will confuse students about whether to declare stock as an instance final field initialized in the constructor or as a static final field at class level.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended design explicit and consistent. Update the problem statement to state one of the two options unambiguously. Recommended change to preserve the current solution: state "Declare private static final Stock stock and initialize it at declaration (or in a static initializer). Initialize the instance orders array in the no-argument constructor." If instead you want per-instance stock, update the note that currently requires stock and related methods to be static and provide examples/tests accordingly.

issues.description: Element: SealSaloon.totalOrders (field). The UML in the problem statement declares totalOrders as type int ("-totalOrders: int"), but the reference implementation declares totalOrders as a long (private long totalOrders = 0;). This type mismatch between the specification diagram and the implementation can confuse students about the expected type and whether to use int or long for totalOrders.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type consistent in teaching materials and template. Either update the UML/problem statement to show "totalOrders: long" or change the reference implementation (and tests, if any) to use int. Prefer updating the UML to long if very large order counts are possible; otherwise prefer int to match the UML and keep examples simple.
